lines: Chronic mid-back pain with night sweats, fatigue, and 6-kg weight loss
The patient with severe alcohol use disorder, chronic pancreatitis, and alcoholic cerebellar degeneration presents with mid-back pain.
He describes the pain as deep and constant, worse at night, and unresponsive to over-the-counter analgesics.
He has also developed night sweats, fatigue, and a 6-kg (13-lb) unintentional weight loss over the last two months.
He has not sought medical care recently and has no known HIV diagnosis.

lines: Severe anxiety, tremors, and profuse sweating 12 hours after quitting alcohol cold turkey

This 53-year-old male with severe alcohol use disorder, chronic pancreatitis with exocrine insufficiency, alcoholic cerebellar degeneration, and alcoholic liver disease returns to the emergency department two months after a previous presentation with confusion and agitation following alcohol cessation.
He now presents with a 12-hour history of increasing anxiety, hand tremors, and profuse sweating.
He reports that he decided to quit drinking alcohol "cold turkey" two days ago after a decade of consuming approximately one pint of vodka daily.
His last drink was 36 hours ago.
